Sorry for dragging this thread out of its grave, but there are two sentences in this that are bothering me. Dunno if the author is still around, but it's worth a shot.

The Foundation's instances of SCP-444 are to be kept under Type A Hazardous documentation protocols.

Shouldn't that be "Type A Hazardous Documentation protocols"? With "documentation" capitalized as well? I read it as if the protocol refers to documentation that is hazardous, and thus, the "documentation" is part of the title.

The mechanism for this change is still unknown.

(Kinda tacked this one on after the other one, but it's less important.) I feel like that would read better as "remains unknown", just based upon what's common in articles these days as opposed to Series I. "Is still" just sounds a little conversational.

item.content:encoded:
Liked this, though the bit about the infant group at the end of the experiment log made me pull a face. (That isn't a criticism, that's just what happened.)

It's interesting to ponder the end-use of this. Obviously whoever was going to use this as an invasion plan would have to A) be able to be understood by their new slaves, B) be able to understand their slaves, C) not get infected by their slaves. So either there must exist a "neutralized" version of SCP-444 that can be learned but is not only non-infectious but also immunizes the one who's learned it, or the creator would have to be immune to the spread in some other way and able to order the slaves around in their original language. Hopefully while still understanding SCP-444, since slaves that you can't actually understand would have limited utility. Utility to be sure, but still limited.

If a non-infectious, immunizing version of 444 exists, the Foundation would want to be hunting it like mad. Of course, there better be someone seriously incorruptible in charge of its recovery and containment, because the temptation for world domination would probably be greater than just about any other SCP out there.
